{{Short description|Condition for polynomials to be unfactorable}}
'''Perron's irreducibility criterion''' is a sufficient condition for a [[polynomial]] to be [[irreducible polynomial|irreducible]] in [[polynomial ring|<math>\mathbb{Z}[x]</math>]]—that is, for it to be unfactorable into the product of lower-[[degree of a polynomial|degree]] polynomials with [[integer]] [[coefficient]]s.

This criterion is applicable only to [[monic polynomial]]s. However, unlike other commonly used criteria, Perron's criterion does not require any knowledge of [[prime decomposition]] of the polynomial's coefficients.

==Criterion==
Suppose we have the following [[polynomial]] with integer coefficients
: <math>f(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0,</math>
where <math>a_0\neq 0</math>. If either of the following two conditions applies:
*<math>|a_{n-1}|> 1+|a_{n-2}|+\cdots+|a_0|</math>
*<math>|a_{n-1}|= 1+|a_{n-2}|+\cdots+|a_0|, \quad f(\pm 1) \neq 0</math>
then <math>f</math> is [[irreducible polynomial|irreducible]] over the integers (and by [[Gauss's lemma (polynomials)|Gauss's lemma]] also over the [[rational number]]s).

==History==
The criterion was first published by [[Oskar Perron]] in 1907 in [[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]].<ref name=Perron>{{cite journal |last=Perron |first=Oskar |author-link=Oskar Perron |title=Neue kriterien für die irreduzibilität algebraischer gleichungen |year=1907 |publisher=Walter de Gruyter |url=https://eudml.org/doc/149269 |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik |volume=132 |pages=288–307}}</ref> 

==Proof==
A short [[mathematical proof|proof]] can be given based on the following [[lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] due to Panaitopol:<ref name=Panaitopol>{{cite book |last1=Panaitopol |first1=Laurențiu |title=Criteriul lui Perron de ireductibilitate a polinoamelor cu coeficienti intregi |year=1993 |publisher=Gazeta Matematică |oclc=6733580644 }}. vol. XCVIII no. 10, 39–340</ref><ref name=Zhao>{{cite web |url=http://yufeizhao.com/olympiad/intpoly.pdf |last=Zhao |first=Yufei |title=Integer Polynomials |year=2007 }}</ref> 

'''Lemma.''' Let <math>f(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0</math> be a polynomial with <math>|a_{n-1}|>1+|a_{n-2}|+\cdots+|a_{1}|+|a_0|</math>. Then exactly one [[root of a polynomial|zero]] <math>z</math> of <math>f</math> satisfies <math>|z|>1</math>, and the other <math>n-1</math> zeroes of <math>f</math> satisfy <math>|z|<1</math>.

Suppose that <math>f(x)=g(x)h(x)</math> where <math>g</math> and <math>h</math> are integer polynomials. Since, by the above lemma, <math>f</math> has only one zero with [[Complex number#Polar complex plane|modulus]] not less than <math>1</math>, one of the polynomials <math>g, h</math> has all its zeroes strictly inside the [[unit circle]]. Suppose that <math>z_1,\dots,z_k</math> are the zeroes of <math>g</math>, and <math>|z_1|,\dots,|z_k|<1</math>. Note that <math>g(0)</math> is a nonzero integer, and <math>|g(0)|=|z_1\cdots z_k|<1</math>, contradiction. Therefore, <math>f</math> is irreducible.

==Generalizations==
In his publication Perron provided variants of the criterion for multivariate polynomials over arbitrary [[field (mathematics)|field]]s. In 2010, Bonciocat published novel proofs of these criteria.<ref name=Bonciocat>{{cite book |last1=Bonciocat |first1=Nicolae  |title=On an irreducibility criterion of Perron for multivariate polynomials |year=2010 |publisher=Societatea de Științe Matematice din România |oclc=6733580644 }}</ref>
